question: A document-processing service receives files that could be invoices, resumes, or contracts, but the type is not known ahead of time. The service defines three separate extraction tools (extract_invoice, extract_resume, extract_contract) and needs Claude to always call exactly one of them so the pipeline never falls back to plain text. Which tool_choice configuration should be used?
options: A) Set tool_choice to {"type": "auto"} so Claude evaluates the document and decides whether calling a tool is appropriate
B) Set tool_choice to {"type": "tool", "name": "extract_invoice"} so the same extraction tool always runs regardless of document type
C) Omit the tools parameter and instruct Claude in the system prompt to always respond using one of the three named JSON shapes
D) Set tool_choice to {"type": "any"} so Claude must call one of the three tools but can pick whichever matches the document
correct_answers: D) Set tool_choice to {"type": "any"} so Claude must call one of the three tools but can pick whichever matches the document
explanations: "auto" is the default and permits Claude to respond with plain text instead of calling any tool, which does not guarantee structured output.
Forcing a single named tool would incorrectly run invoice extraction even on resumes or contracts, since the document type is unknown in advance.
Without the tools parameter there is no schema enforcement at all; Claude would be generating free-form text that happens to look like JSON, reintroducing syntax risk.

Correct. tool_choice: "any" forces Claude to call some tool but leaves the choice of which tool up to the model, which is exactly what's needed when the document type is unknown but a tool call must always happen.
